evidence.quote: Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire replied “Very cool” to AStock's post announcing the upcoming launch of Omni Launchpad. This interaction naturally draws a connection between Circle, Arc, and the tokenized stock ecosystem. After all, AStock is built on Arc, the financial infrastructure developed by Circle.

AStock has announced that Omni Launchpad will launch across both Arc and Solana, with the goal of allowing a token to be issued and circulated across both ecosystems. The announced features include configurable trading taxes for developers, optional stock rewards for holders with the ability to select the corresponding stock, two-way transfers between Arc

However, the current announcement only confirms that product testing has been completed and that the launch is approaching. Actual cross-chain trading volume, the full details of Ferry's yield mechanism, and Omni's long-term revenue have yet to be demonstrated. These will need to be verified after launch.

The latest website data already shows some actual usage: approximately $61,704.76 in stock assets has been distributed to holders, around $5,336.02 in USDC entered the reward pool that day, and the most recent distribution involved 1,787 wallets.

In terms of burns, approximately 78.03M ASTOCK has been burned, representing 7.80% of total supply. The website also shows approximately $10,437.07 spent on buybacks and burns, corresponding to 11.44M ASTOCK.

What I really want to see is this: How many projects with no direct connection to AStock will eventually choose to route their fees into this stock rewards system? That will be the key indicator of whether AStock can build a genuine network effect.

My overall view: fundamentals are strengthening, but the short-term price is clearly overheated. This rally is being driven by both product expansion and external attention. The next thing to validate is Omni's actual adoption, rather than treating Jeremy's “Very cool” comment as a long-term fundamental catalyst in itself.

items.author: hansolar21
items.new_information: 六项筛选标准及刷分成本与证伪条件

evidence.quote: His six criteria:
◾️ Organic usage : Sustained volume and OI across multiple timeframes, not just incentive-driven spikes.
◾️ Product differentiation : Something traders will actually want to use after the points end.
◾️ Tokenomics : Circulating float, supply dynamics, and distribution policy.
◾️ Liquidity edge : A sustainable advantage in liquidity and execution quality.
◾️ Business model : Real revenue and a credible path to profitability.
◾️ Timing : Getting in early enough for the risk/reward to make sense.

If you need to trade repeatedly to earn points, even small execution costs can accumulate. A points program that looks lucrative on paper may be less attractive once you account for the actual cost of participation.
The best opportunity isn't necessarily the protocol offering the most points. It's the one where the potential reward makes sense relative to the cost, risk and uncertainty involved.
Instead, define your thesis before you become attached to the outcome.

evidence.quote: We asked GPT-6 Astra to edit Qwen3.5-0.8B weights to improve math.
